last_done_increment.summary: 2026-07-12: the 'GloSource Verified' badge sat only on three mega-ODMs, so an indie brand with a 1,000-unit budget was being pointed at factories that would not take their order — a trust claim we cannot cash. Curated four more K-Beauty manufacturers using the product's own method: web discovery, then cross-check against the government registries we already ingest (MFDS kr_cosmetics_firms induty=화장품제조 for the manufacturing licence + business-reg number + plant address; MFDS CGMP list matched on business-reg number). The registry did real work and rejected most of what the web calls a low-MOQ Korean factory: Laonhase advertises the lowest MOQ anyone does (300 units) yet has NO MFDS manufacturing record under that name (exactly the trap our buyers fall into); Factosquare is 화장품책임판매 only (a brand owner); Selfcos and Smallcosmetic have no record at all; OEMKorea/CosKorea/Crescent Seoul/Mayk/Sourcing Lab/KPrivateLabel are sourcing agencies that outrank real factories and resell someone else's plant. Survivors: NOWCOS and Hankook Cosmo (CGMP-certified, mid-size, publish no MOQ) and COSMEDIQUE and CTK (publish a 1,000-unit MOQ but are NOT CGMP-listed) — the notes state that trade-off plainly rather than implying every badged supplier is both cheap to start with and top-certified. COSMAX was corrected, not just kept: its 2023 indie programme dropped the minimum from 10,000 to 1,000 units, so the old 'typically high MOQ' note had been steering away the exact buyer it was meant to help; the seed now upserts instead of skipping, or a stale note would survive forever precisely because the row exists. Critically, seeding alone changed NOTHING for buyers: dbFallbackOutput injected only two curated rows with no ORDER BY, so insertion order handed every search to the mega-ODMs — fixed in a4c4b76 (MOQ ascending, NULLS LAST) and verified against the production table (a serum query now injects COSMAX 1,000 + COSMEDIQUE 1,000). 6 new honesty-invariant tests: a CGMP claim must match the government list by business-reg number, an MOQ must be the company's own published figure or null, trustScore stays null, and the rejected middlemen cannot reappear. Green: tsc, eslint (0 errors), npm test 25/25, next build. Prior increments this branch: GLO-EN-JSONLD-PRICE (8306d94), GLO-EN-TRUSTANCHOR (7abe07a), GLO-EN-PAYHIST (406b411), GLO-HARDEN (a1e8f62).

Resolved 2026-07-11 (cdaae3d): .github/workflows/promote.yml runs build + tests on every branch push and fast-forwards master only when they pass, which Vercel then deploys. Merge is no longer a human gate; a red build is the gate. Escape hatch [no-promote] is read from the commit subject line only.

Resolved 2026-07-12 (GLO-EN-DBSEED-EXPAND, seeded to prod with operator approval): a serum query now injects two factories that publish a 1,000-unit minimum an indie brand can meet (COSMAX's 2023 indie programme + COSMEDIQUE), instead of mega-ODMs whose minimum nobody published. Every badged row cites its MFDS manufacturing licence and business-reg number, and a CGMP claim is test-checked against the government list.

The 20 K-Food / K-Fashion rows (addedBy=harness:curate-fallback) carry the same 'GloSource Verified' badge but have null MOQ and were never cross-checked against a government registry (HACCP for food; none ingested for fashion).
